text.p: Top Palestinian peace negotiator Mahmoud Abbas has resigned from heading PLO talks with Israel over what a key aide said on Monday was the Jewish state's intransigence.
Abbas, better known as Abu Mazen, handed Palestinian President Yasser Arafat his resignation letter after a tough meeting with Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy late on Sunday.
"Abu Mazen's resignation letter has been placed on the table of President Arafat," said Arafat's aide Ahmed Tibi.
"Abu Mazen is tired of these one-sided Israeli decisions -- the settlement at Har Homa, the closing of offices and the recent rededployment decision," he told Israel's army radio.
The radio said Arafat had not decided if to accept the resignation. Abbas could not immediately be reached for comment.

Israel angered Palestinians last week with its decision to hand over nine percent of the West Bank in the first of three withdrawals outlined in a peace agreement. Palestinians say they were expecting 30 percent of the land.

The decision came on the heels of two other Israeli moves which irked Palestinians -- the approval to build a new Jewish neighbourhood in Arab East Jerusalem and the decision to shut down four PLO offices in East Jerusalem.
Abbas led Palestinian negotiators in talks with Israel that produced the breakthrough 1993 Israel-PLO peace accord.
An Israeli official said on Wednesday Israel would not go ahead with its planned withdrawal as long as the Palestinian Authority refused to cooperate.
